## Why plant-disease localization matters

- Crop losses from disease: **20–40 %** of global production.
- Precision agriculture stack already deploys UAVs + IoT detectors.
- Actionable use (severity, targeted spraying, monitoring) needs **spatial lesion masks**, not just a "diseased/healthy" tag.

**Visual:** 2×3 grid of PlantSeg images + GT masks (apple black rot, grape leaf spot, tomato bacterial spot, corn gray leaf spot, healthy leaf for contrast).

## The annotation crisis

- Fully-supervised CV needs **dense per-pixel masks** drawn by domain experts.
- In a narrow domain like plant pathology: small budgets, scarce annotators, ambiguous lesion boundaries.
- Largest public pixel-annotated dataset (**PlantSeg**, ~7.7 k images, 116 classes) released **late 2025**.

**Visual:** vertical infographic — three large numbers ("20–40 % yield loss", "7.7 k pixel-annotated images", "released late 2025").

## Alternatives to dense annotation

- Transfer learning.
- Active learning.
- Self-supervised pretraining.
- **Weakly-supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS)** — masks from image-level labels only.
- WSSS is the most attractive: image-level disease labels are already abundant (PlantVillage: 54 k images, image-level only).

**Visual:** 4-quadrant comparison panel — one paradigm per quadrant with a one-line definition and a representative paper.

## WSSS lives on PASCAL VOC — and that's a problem

- Published WSSS methods almost exclusively benchmarked on **PASCAL VOC** (or COCO).
- PASCAL VOC SOTA: **60–75 % mIoU** — looks "almost solved".
- Transfer to specialised domains is much weaker than headlines suggest.
- This thesis quantifies that gap.

**Visual:** horizontal bar — *PASCAL VOC WSSS: 60–75 % mIoU* → *plant-disease WSSS (this work): 33.3 % disease IoU*.

## Goal

> Adapt weakly-supervised semantic segmentation to the narrow domain of plant-disease localization, and quantify what can and cannot be achieved when only image-level labels are available.

**Visual:** the goal sentence as a single coloured callout box; no other content.

## Tasks

1. Collect datasets and build a reproducible data pipeline.
2. Reproduce, evaluate and adapt SOTA WSSS methods on the plant-disease domain.
3. Estimate a principled **upper bound** on what WSSS can extract — and design the estimation procedure.
4. Introduce **shallow signal probing** as the instrument for (3).

**Visual:** horizontal flowchart — Datasets → Reproduction → Upper-bound estimation → Shallow probing — arrow into "Quantitative findings + null results".

## Datasets

- **PlantSeg v3** — primary; in-the-wild; pixel + image-level GT.
- **PlantVillage** — auxiliary weak-supervision source; image-level labels only.
- **PASCAL VOC 2012** — sanity-check reproduction.

**Visual:** table — *Dataset / Role / # Images / # Classes / Supervision* (three rows). Below it, two example images side by side (PlantSeg lesion vs PASCAL whole object) to make the visual gap obvious.

## Methods — families covered

- Classical CAM (GradCAM + CRF).
- CAM + pixel affinity (PSA / AffinityNet + Random Walk).
- Transformer-based (MCTformer).
- Foundation-model assisted (WeakCLIP, SAM-prompted CAM).
- Siamese (SPDNet ADPL-CAM + our spatial cross-attention).
- Fully-supervised upper bound (SegNeXt).

**Visual:** taxonomy diagram — five family boxes feeding into a single "evaluated on PlantSeg" pipe.

## PASCAL VOC sanity check vs PlantSeg transfer

- Reproduced numbers match papers within **~1–2 pp on PASCAL VOC**.
- Drop **25–35 pp** when transferred to PlantSeg.
- Gap is consistent across families — not a tuning artefact.

**Visual:** full-width table.

| Family | Method | VOC mIoU (paper) | VOC mIoU (reprod.) | PlantSeg disease IoU |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CAM | GradCAM + CRF |  |  |  |
| CAM + affinity | PSA + Random Walk |  |  |  |
| Transformer | MCTformer |  |  |  |
| Foundation | WeakCLIP |  |  |  |
| Foundation | SAM-prompted CAM |  |  |  |
| Siamese | SPDNet (ADPL-CAM) |  |  |  |
| Siamese (ours) | SPDNet + spatial X-attn |  |  |  |
| Supervised UB | SegNeXt | — | — |  |

## SPDNet — what & why it is promising

- Closest published WSSS architecture to the plant-disease domain.
- Siamese reference-guided attention: a healthy reference patch anchors the attention on the diseased query.
- Plant lesions = local deviations from healthy tissue → Siamese framing matches the problem geometry.
- We extend SPDNet with a new **spatial cross-attention** variant on top of the original ADPL-CAM token fusion.

**Visual:** SPDNet architecture diagram (query + reference branches → spatial X-attn block → classifier head → CAM output). New module highlighted.

## SPDNet — experimental setups tried

- 448² baseline training.
- 896² high-resolution training + four "scale trap" fixes (LR rule, scale-aware `ref_pool_size`, `min_lr` floor, val-transform).
- `ref_pool_size` sweep: rps ∈ {14, 20, 56}.
- Mask supervision: cls-only → warm-start + L_mask.
- Auxiliary losses: L_eq, L_con, L_distill.

**Visual:** compact 5-row "experiment grid" table — *Setup / Knob varied / Outcome (one word: ✓ / null / mixed)*.

## SPDNet — results

- Best end-to-end WSSS: **disease IoU = 33.94 %** (SPDNet + L_mask, multi-scale + CRF).
- `ref_pool_size` is **saturated for classification** but **leveraged for mask supervision**.
- L_eq → clean **null result** (attention collapse to uniform).
- High-resolution naïve scaling → strictly worse than 448 without the trap fixes.

**Visual:** bar chart — disease IoU across cls-only, +L_mask, +L_mask+L_eq, supervised UB.

## Shallow probes — concept

- Standard CAM shows what the **classifier head** chose to emphasise.
- Question: how much localization signal is **already latent** in the features?
- A **shallow probe** is a 2-layer 1×1-conv decoder attached to a frozen intermediate layer and trained on the (small) pixel-labelled probe split.
- Probe IoU = experimentally tractable **upper bound** on any unsupervised aggregation of the same features.

**Visual:** schematic — frozen backbone → tap at layer L → trained probe head → predicted mask → IoU vs GT. Probe head highlighted as "the only trainable block".

## Shallow probes — headline result

- Production CAM + CRF ceiling on SPDNet features: **~32 % disease IoU**.
- Shallow probe on the same features: **42–62 % disease IoU**.
- The localization signal exists — the **readout** is throwing it away.
- ~25× larger gain than anything mask supervision or auxiliary losses produced.

**Visual:** line plot — probe disease IoU vs network depth; horizontal dashed lines at the CAM ceiling (~32 %) and the supervised SegNeXt upper bound (~70 %).

## Why the PASCAL VOC recipe transfers poorly

- **Lesion sparsity & scale.** PlantSeg lesions are small, sparse, low-contrast — CAMs latch onto the most discriminative patch, missing diffuse regions.
- **Foundation models are domain-shifted.** CLIP & SAM trained on web-scale general imagery → severe **oversegmentation** on plant lesions.
- **Aux losses have trivial fixed points.** L_eq, L_ac admit spatially-uniform attention as a global minimum on the loss alone.

**Visual:** none — three terse bullets only.

## Domain-gap — qualitative failure panel

**Visual (whole-slide figure, minimal text):**

- 4-panel comparison on one PlantSeg image:
  - col 1: GT lesion mask;
  - col 2: CLIP-prompted segmentation (oversegmented, latches onto leaf);
  - col 3: SAM-prompted segmentation (segments the whole leaf);
  - col 4: our best WSSS output.
- One-line caption — *"foundation-model priors do not transfer to plant lesions"*.

## Contributions

- Reproducible PlantSeg + PlantVillage data pipeline (MLflow + DVC tracked).
- Calibrated PlantSeg benchmark across 7 WSSS methods + supervised upper bound.
- **Shallow-probe localization-capacity methodology** — reusable beyond this domain.
- Documented null results: L_eq, L_con, naïve high-res scaling, CLIP/SAM-prompted refinement.

**Visual:** 4-row contribution table — *Task → Contribution → Headline number / artefact*.

## Take-home message

- WSSS in narrow scientific domains is genuinely hard — not a solved problem.
- The bottleneck is the **readout**, not the representation.
- The shallow probe is the right tool to expose that bottleneck.
- Negative-but-rigorous map of the plant-disease WSSS landscape, motivated by crop preservation and food security.

**Visual:** one-sentence callout box with the punchline. Faded version of the Slide 3 lesion grid as a thematic bookend.
